definition: An adventitial fibroblast representing the immune-interacting, paracrine pole of the universal fibroblast continuum, characterised by high expression of collagen XV alpha 1 (COL15A1), complement component C7, and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12 (CXCL12) in humans, and variably expressing C3 and ABCA10 (Cohen et al., 2026; DOI:10.64898/2026.06.10.731198). This cell colocalises with lymphocytes and inflammatory macrophages, organising perivascular immune niches, and is the differentiated counterpart to the PI16-high progenitor pole of the universal fibroblast continuum (Zeltz et al., 2022; DOI:10.1007/s12079-022-00673-3; Yang et al., 2026; DOI:10.1172/jci.insight.202529). It is distinguished from mural cells by absence of CSPG4, MCAM, RGS5, and ACTA2 (Yang et al., 2026).

logical_axioms.notes: CXCL12+/COL15A1+ adventitial fibroblasts occupy adventitial and perivaascular positions across organs including fallopian tube, ovary, and myometrium (Cohen et al. 2026). CURATOR REVIEW NEEDED: Zeltz et al. (2022) report that COL15A1+ universal fibroblasts are found deeper in parenchymal tissues, not exclusively in the perivascular adventitia; this axiom may therefore overclaim adventitial restriction. The CXCL12+ immune-niche identity is adventitial but the COL15A1 marker axis may extend beyond the tunica adventitia. Recommend CL curators review whether a broader anatomical filler (e.g. connective tissue) is more appropriate, or whether this axiom should be qualified.

COL15A1+ adventitial fibroblasts are described as basement-membrane-secreting universal fibroblasts (Obacz et al. 2022; Zeltz et al. 2022); extracellular matrix organization is a core defining function shared with the PI16+ pole but reflected in the COL15A1 (collagen XV) expression.

references.supports: Atlas identification of CXCL12+/COL15A1+ pole (Mesen_AdvFibs_PI16low: C3, ABCA10, C7; Mesen_AdvFibsIntr: ACSM3, C7); distribution across fallopian tube mucosa, ovarian subserosa, and myometrial adventitia; transcriptional continuum from PI16hi to C7/COL15A1hi; immune-niche colocalisation with lymphocytes and macrophages

Two pan-tissue universal fibroblast archetypes (PI16+ perivascular vs COL15A1+ parenchymal/basement-membrane-associated); COL15A1+ fibroblasts noted deeper inside parenchymal tissues — key basis for the caveat about adventitial restriction
COL15A1+ as the second universal fibroblast subtype; distinguishing absence of mural markers CSPG4, MCAM, RGS5, ACTA2; cross-tissue distribution
PI16-/COL15A1+ cells proposed as universal parenchymal fibroblasts secreting basement membranes; explicit distinction from PI16+ adventitial fibroblasts; DPT co-expression

CXCL12+ stromal niche fibroblasts described as the immune-interacting, paracrine pole of the universal fibroblast continuum, colocalising with lymphocytes and inflammatory macrophages — deepsearch source, DOI not yet confirmed in catalogue

Identification of immune-activated fibroblast subclusters (HLA-DRA/CD74+) in asthma bronchial tissue as the differentiated/niche-forming counterpart to matrix/vascular fibroblasts — deepsearch source, DOI not yet confirmed in catalogue
Perivascular adventitial fibroblast specialisation accompanying T cell retention in inflamed human dermis — supports immune-niche role of adventitial fibroblasts

justification:
CL:4052030 (adventitial fibroblast) has no molecular characterisation and no children other than a single artery-location term (CL:1000306). The CXCL12+/COL15A1+ adventitial fibroblast is the second of two reproducible, cross-tissue universal fibroblast archetypes — the immune-interacting, differentiated counterpart to the PI16-high progenitor pole (drafted separately as 'PI16-high adventitial fibroblast'). It is identified across reproductive, pulmonary, dermal, and vascular atlases by COL15A1, C7, and CXCL12 co-expression, colocalisaton with perivascular immune cells, and absence of mural markers. Neither this marker profile nor the immune-niche identity is captured by any existing CL term.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR CL CURATORS: The assignment of this term as a child of CL:4052030 (adventitial fibroblast) requires review. Zeltz et al. (2022; DOI:10.1007/s12079-022-00673-3) report that COL15A1+ universal fibroblasts occupy deeper parenchymal positions rather than the perivascular adventitia — in contrast to PI16+ fibroblasts, which are perivascular. Cohen et al. (2026) in the reproductive atlas atlas find the C7/COL15A1hi state distributed across mucosal interstitium, ovarian subserosa, and adventitial positions around vasculature — a broader anatomical footprint than the PI16hi state (99% fallopian tube subserosa). The CXCL12+ immune-niche identity is adventitial in the reproductive atlas context (Levy-Lambert 2025), but the COL15A1 marker axis may extend beyond the tunica adventitia of blood vessels. Curators should consider whether: (a) the parent should remain CL:4052030 with a qualifying note; (b) a broader parent (e.g. fibroblast) is more appropriate; or (c) the term should carry two separate anatomical location axioms (adventitial + parenchymal connective tissue). This tension is stated plainly and the term is not overclaiming adventitial restriction.

Proposed logical axioms:
- subClassOf 'part of' some 'tunica adventitia of blood vessel' (UBERON:0005734) — subject to curator review of COL15A1+ anatomical scope
- subClassOf 'capable of' some 'extracellular matrix organization' (GO:0030198) — COL15A1/collagen XV expression and basement-membrane secretion

Implicit immune-niche function (colocalisation with lymphocytes, paracrine signalling via CXCL12) is described in the definition text. A 'capable of chemokine production' or 'capable of lymphocyte chemotaxis' axiom would be appropriate but is not proposed here as a verified GO CURIE was not confirmed from the available evidence files; curators should add if warranted.

**Additional notes or concerns**
This term captures the CXCL12+/COL15A1+ pole of the universal fibroblast, the immune-interacting, differentiated counterpart to the PI16-high progenitor pole (requested separately as 'PI16-high adventitial fibroblast'). The two poles together constitute the universal fibroblast pair that is reproducibly recovered across human single-cell atlases of lung, skin, artery, gut, reproductive tract, pleura, and tonsil.

In the HCA reproductive atlas (Cohen et al. 2026), the COL15A1hi state comprises two clusters: Mesen_AdvFibs_PI16low (markers: C3, ABCA10, C7) and Mesen_AdvFibsIntr (markers: ACSM3, C7). Together these are distributed across the fallopian tube mucosal interstitium, the subserosa beneath the ovarian surface epithelium, and adventitial positions around vasculature in the ovary, fallopian tube, and myometrium — a broader anatomical footprint than the PI16hi state (99% fallopian tube subserosa).

This cell is distinguished from its PI16-high sibling by: absence of high PI16/DPP4/CD34; presence of COL15A1/C7/CXCL12; immune-niche colocalisation; differentiated (rather than quiescent progenitor) state. It is distinguished from mural cells by absence of CSPG4/NG2, MCAM/CD146, RGS5, and ACTA2.

**IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR CL CURATORS — adventitial parentage requires review:**
Zeltz et al. (2022; DOI:10.1007/s12079-022-00673-3) report that COL15A1+ universal fibroblasts (Col15a1+ in mice) sit deeper in parenchymal tissues, not in perivascular niches — the opposite distribution from PI16+ fibroblasts. This means the COL15A1+ pole is not reliably adventitial, and placing this term under CL:4052030 (adventitial fibroblast, defined as 'a fibroblast of the adventitia of a blood vessel') may not be appropriate. The CXCL12+ immune-niche identity is adventitial in the reproductive atlas (Levy-Lambert et al. 2025), but the COL15A1 marker axis extends beyond the adventitia. Curators should decide whether: (a) the parent remains CL:4052030 with a qualifying note; (b) a broader parent (fibroblast, CL:0000057) is more appropriate; or (c) the term should carry two anatomical location axioms. This tension is stated explicitly and the term does not overclaim adventitial restriction.

Proposed logical axioms:
- subClassOf 'part of' some 'tunica adventitia of blood vessel' (UBERON:0005734) — subject to curator review of COL15A1+ anatomical scope (see caveat above)
- subClassOf 'capable of' some 'extracellular matrix organization' (GO:0030198) — COL15A1/collagen XV expression and basement-membrane secretion

The immune-niche role (CXCL12-mediated lymphocyte attraction, colocalisation with macrophages) is described in the definition text. A 'capable of' axiom for chemokine production or lymphocyte chemotaxis would be appropriate but is deferred to curator verification of the relevant GO CURIE.
